subject: Gen5 Lane D complete: 120 Hz is incremental; direct-vsync virtual presentation is the larger latency lever
body: Lane D research complete against main bfbf5d68fc84cab62cadcbc0b6bc5eefbc7ba5ea. Confirmed: current overlay params do not request a refresh rate; FoldOverlayView already scales the expensive shader specifically with 120 Hz cost in mind; current Fold7 continuity opening uses TiltFollower with CONTINUITY_OPENING_TAU_S=0.09s; TiltFollower's first callback hard-codes dt=1/60 when no prior timestamp; Fold7 live blur remains disabled and should stay off for the high-cadence path. Deterministic timing model: 60->120 Hz reduces mean next-vsync wait 8.33->4.17 ms (4.17 ms gain), P95 15.83->7.92 ms, worst 16.67->8.33 ms. By contrast a 90 ms first-order follower has ~62.38 ms half-response, validating the principal design requirement to bypass legacy smoothing for trusted direct-vsync virtual output. Platform recommendation: visual-attempt-scoped 120 Hz lease; one setFrameRate request using FRAME_RATE_COMPATIBILITY_DEFAULT + CHANGE_FRAME_RATE_ONLY_IF_SEAMLESS, verify actual cadence, clear with 0 Hz at lease end; never CHANGE_FRAME_RATE_ALWAYS. Strong Gen5 host option on Fold7/Android16: API34+ SurfaceControlViewHost + AccessibilityService.attachAccessibilityOverlayToDisplay for a public SurfaceControl and atomic frame-rate/visual transactions, with existing WindowManager overlay fallback.
